primary_claim: When clue complexity is high enough that the model needs its CoT to decode it, models are almost always faithful under a relaxed definition (>97%, with confirmed unfaithfulness on at most 1-2% of runs), and a simple LLM-based Clue-Usage Detector can distinguish clue-usage from genuine problem-solving via the CoT with 99.3% TPR at 96.2% specificity, robust to modest adversarial prompting intended to obfuscate the CoT

effect.metric: relaxed CoT-faithfulness rate; Clue-Usage Detector TPR at fixed specificity
effect.value: relaxed faithfulness >97% on non-trivial clues (confirmed unfaithfulness on at most ~1-2% of runs); Detector TPR 99.3% at 96.2% specificity, averaged across models/clues/prompts

contradicts_or_qualifies: prior work (arXiv:2305.04388; Anthropic Claude 3.7/4 system cards) showing low CoT faithfulness under a strict definition; this post argues that under a relaxed, information-sufficiency definition, and when reasoning genuinely requires CoT, models are highly faithful and detectable, qualifying the earlier pessimistic framing
stated_future_work: explore RL-based elicitation of models' CoT-obfuscation ability, in addition to prompting
develop better/more thorough CoT behavior detectors and analysis strategies
investigate how to preserve natural-language meaning in the CoT under RL training, including training on paraphrased CoT
test more natural task settings such as ControlArena side objectives instead of artificial clues
develop model organisms of CoT obfuscation to validate these evaluations
limitations_stated: no ground truth about LLMs' true internal cognitive processes, so validity of faithfulness/detector metrics is hard to establish
clue-using and non-clue-using trajectories come from systematically different prompt/problem distributions rather than the same distribution
eliciting both the target cognitive behavior and the model's obfuscation capability via prompting alone may not fully elicit true obfuscation capability
the 'clue usage' setup is an artificial analog for real dangerous behaviors and may not generalize to natural, real-world CoT monitoring
prompting to elicit clue usage caused unusual CoT artifacts that likely made detection artificially easy
quote: It was relatively straightforward to build an automatic detector with a True Positive Rate of 99.3% across all clues, models, and prompts (at 96.2% specificity).
